seo.title: Lyabi Hauz Teahouse in Bukhara (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover the best lyabi hauz teahouse in Bukhara for 2026 — curated picks with maps, hours, and insider tips.

hero.h1: Sip green tea and eat shashlik beside the ancient Lyabi-Hauz pool, once a caravan crossroads at the heart of the Silk Road city of Bukhara.
hero.subtitle: Experience Bukhara's timeless charm by dining al fresco at Lyabi-Hauz, where ancient trade routes meet exquisite local flavors of grilled meats and fragrant teas.

picks.name: Chaykhana Lyabi Hauz
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located directly on the banks of the Lyabi-Hauz pool, this chaykhana offers unparalleled views and a truly authentic Silk Road ambiance. Enjoy your meal under ancient mulberry trees, serenaded by the gentle sounds of the bustling square. It's an iconic spot for both locals and travelers.
picks.whatToOrder: Shashlik assorti (mixed skewers) with a pot of Kok Choy (green tea)
picks.insiderTip: Arrive just before sunset to secure a prime table and watch the square come alive with evening lights, creating a magical dining experience.
picks.redditQuote: "You *have* to eat at Chaykhana Lyabi Hauz. The shashlik is fantastic, and sitting right there by the pool as the sun sets is peak Bukhara."

picks.name: Old Bukhara Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Set in a beautifully restored traditional house just steps from Lyabi-Hauz, Old Bukhara offers a more refined yet equally authentic experience. They are renowned for their flavorful shashlik and often feature live Uzbek music and dance performances in the evenings, enhancing the cultural immersion.
picks.whatToOrder: Lamb shashlik and a pot of Black Tea with local sweets
picks.insiderTip: Book ahead, especially for dinner, if you want a table with a good view of the stage for the live music. The atmosphere is vibrant but popular.
picks.redditQuote: "Old Bukhara Restaurant exceeded expectations! The lamb shashlik was tender, and the live music made the evening unforgettable. A must-visit."

picks.name: Rustam & Zukhra Teahouse
picks.neighborhood: Old City, near Nadir Divan-Beghi Madrasah
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A charming, family-run teahouse known for its warm hospitality and delicious homemade food. While primarily a teahouse, they serve excellent, freshly grilled shashlik alongside an extensive menu of local dishes. It's a cozy spot for a more intimate dining experience away from the main square's bustle.
picks.whatToOrder: Chicken shashlik with a variety of infused green teas (e.g., lemon-mint)
picks.insiderTip: Don't miss trying their homemade samsa or somsa (savory pastries) if available; they pair wonderfully with the tea.
picks.redditQuote: "Rustam & Zukhra Teahouse felt like eating at a local's home. The shashlik was fantastic, and their tea selection is huge. Super cozy vibes."

picks.name: Labi Hovuz Chaikhana
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Another excellent choice right on the Lyabi-Hauz square, offering a slightly more casual setting than its immediate neighbors. It's a great spot for people-watching while enjoying traditional Uzbek fare. Their shashlik is consistently good, and the service is efficient, making it ideal for a relaxed meal.
picks.whatToOrder: Beef shashlik and a classic pot of Pialla Choy (black tea)
picks.insiderTip: They have outdoor seating directly facing the pool, which is lovely during the day. Consider it for a leisurely lunch or early dinner to avoid the peak evening crowds.
picks.redditQuote: "Labi Hovuz Chaikhana was my go-to for a quick, tasty shashlik and tea lunch right on the square. No fuss, just good food and a great view."

picks.name: Doston House Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: While famous for its Plov, Doston House also serves excellent shashlik in a traditional courtyard setting. Located a short walk from Lyabi-Hauz, it offers a slightly quieter atmosphere. The food is prepared with fresh, local ingredients, and the portions are generous, reflecting true Uzbek hospitality.
picks.whatToOrder: Assorted shashlik skewers (lamb, beef, chicken) and a pot of Kukk Choy (green tea)
picks.insiderTip: Visit during lunchtime for their legendary Plov, but don't overlook their shashlik, which is expertly grilled and incredibly flavorful. It's a good alternative if Lyabi-Hauz is too crowded.
picks.redditQuote: "We went to Doston House for Plov, but their shashlik was surprisingly good too! Definitely worth the short walk from Lyabi-Hauz for a more local vibe."

picks.name: Mulla Kholiq Chaykhana
picks.neighborhood: Old City, close to Poi Kalyan Complex
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A less tourist-centric chaykhana, Mulla Kholiq offers an authentic local experience with very reasonable prices. It might be a little further walk from Lyabi-Hauz, but the quality of the shashlik and the robust flavor of their green tea are worth it. Expect a bustling, no-frills environment popular with Bukhara residents.
picks.whatToOrder: Mix shashlik (liver and meat) and a large pot of traditional green tea
picks.insiderTip: This is a great option for experiencing local life. Don't be shy to point at what others are eating if you're unsure what to order. Cash is often preferred here.
picks.redditQuote: "If you want real local shashlik without the tourist premium, Mulla Kholiq Chaykhana is the spot. It's a bit of a walk but totally worth it for the authenticity."

picks.name: Café Wishbone
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A modern and stylish cafe offering a fusion of Uzbek and European dishes, including excellent shashlik. While it has a contemporary feel, it retains traditional elements and is a comfortable spot to enjoy a meal. It's a good choice if you're looking for a slightly different ambiance than the traditional chaykhana.
picks.whatToOrder: Beef shashlik and an iced green tea (if you need a break from hot tea)
picks.insiderTip: They offer reliable Wi-Fi, making it a good place to relax and catch up after exploring the sights. Their salads are also fresh and tasty.
picks.redditQuote: "Café Wishbone was a nice change of pace. Their shashlik was surprisingly good and the atmosphere was more modern. Plus, good coffee alongside traditional tea!"

picks.name: Chor Minor Restaurant & Tea House
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Nestled near the picturesque Chor Minor madrasah, this charming establishment offers a tranquil dining experience. Its location allows for a peaceful escape from the main crowds while still being steeped in history. They serve excellent grilled meats and a fine selection of teas in a cozy, traditionally decorated interior.
picks.whatToOrder: Lamb Kebab (shashlik) and a pot of green tea with local herbs
picks.insiderTip: After your meal, take a short stroll to admire the unique four minarets of Chor Minor, especially beautiful under the soft evening lights.
picks.redditQuote: "Found Chor Minor Restaurant after visiting the madrasah and loved it. Quiet, great shashlik, and a nice relaxed atmosphere. Highly recommend the herbal tea."

picks.name: Samani Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Set within a beautifully restored caravanserai courtyard, Samani Restaurant offers a unique dining experience just a stone's throw from Lyabi-Hauz. The historic setting adds a special ambiance to your meal of expertly prepared shashlik and aromatic green tea. It's a fantastic spot for dinner.
picks.whatToOrder: Mixed Grill Platter (includes various shashliks) and a pot of Jasmine Green Tea
picks.insiderTip: Explore the adjacent souvenir shops within the caravanserai before or after your meal – they offer unique local crafts and textiles.
picks.redditQuote: "Samani Restaurant had incredible ambiance, dining in an old caravanserai courtyard was so cool! The shashlik was perfectly cooked and tea was refreshing."

picks.name: Anor Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Anor Restaurant presents a more upscale take on Uzbek cuisine, combining traditional flavors with modern presentation. While they offer a full menu, their shashlik is a standout, grilled to perfection and served elegantly. It's an excellent choice for a special evening out, still within easy reach of Lyabi-Hauz.
picks.whatToOrder: Pomegranate-glazed Lamb Shashlik and their signature 'Anor Choy' (pomegranate tea)
picks.insiderTip: Their dessert menu is quite creative, offering a modern twist on traditional Uzbek sweets. It's a nice way to end a delicious meal.
picks.redditQuote: "Anor Restaurant was a bit pricier but the quality was evident. The shashlik was amazing, and the pomegranate tea was a unique touch. Felt very special."

picks.name: Naqshband Garden Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Enjoy your shashlik and tea in a serene garden setting at Naqshband. This restaurant is known for its beautiful outdoor seating and tranquil atmosphere, making it a peaceful retreat. They offer a good selection of freshly grilled meats and a variety of green teas, including some with local herbs.
picks.whatToOrder: Vegetable Shashlik (for non-meat eaters) or Mixed Lamb & Beef Shashlik, with a pot of refreshing green tea
picks.insiderTip: The garden is particularly lovely during the warmer months. If you're looking for a quiet, leafy spot away from the direct bustle of Lyabi-Hauz, this is it.
picks.redditQuote: "Naqshband Garden was a delightful surprise. Eating shashlik in that peaceful garden felt like a true oasis. The tea was perfect after a long day."

picks.name: Chaykhana Khonakoh
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A no-frills, authentic chaykhana a bit further into the Old City, offering a genuine local experience. While not directly on Lyabi-Hauz, it's easily accessible and provides excellent value. Their shashlik is tender and flavorful, and the green tea is served in the traditional manner, ensuring a true taste of Bukhara.
picks.whatToOrder: Jigar Shashlik (liver shashlik, a local favorite) and a pot of pure Kok Choy
picks.insiderTip: This chaykhana is popular with locals, so expect a lively atmosphere, especially during lunch hours. It's a great place to observe daily Bukhara life.
picks.redditQuote: "If you're willing to walk a bit, Chaykhana Khonakoh is legit. Best liver shashlik I had in Bukhara, and the tea never stops coming."

faq.question: What makes Lyabi-Hauz a special place to eat shashlik and drink green tea?
faq.answer: Lyabi-Hauz is the heart of Bukhara's Old City, an ancient plaza centered around a historic pool, once a vital water source and meeting point on the Silk Road. Dining here under ancient mulberry trees, surrounded by centuries-old madrasahs and khanqas, immerses you in the city's rich history and vibrant culture, creating an unforgettable sensory experience.

faq.question: What is shashlik and how is it traditionally prepared in Bukhara?
faq.answer: Shashlik refers to skewered and grilled meat, a staple in Central Asian cuisine. In Bukhara, it's typically made with lamb, beef, or chicken, often marinated overnight in a mixture of onions, spices, and sometimes vinegar or lemon juice. It's then cooked over an open flame until tender and slightly charred, usually served with fresh onions and a side of flatbread (non).

faq.question: What types of green tea are commonly served in Bukhara?
faq.answer: In Bukhara, green tea (Kok Choy) is ubiquitous and served hot, without milk or sugar, as a gesture of hospitality. Common varieties include pure green tea, often with a subtle grassy or floral note, and sometimes flavored with local herbs like mint or lemon. Black tea (Pialla Choy) is also popular, especially during colder months.

faq.question: Is it safe to eat street food or shashlik from smaller local vendors in Bukhara?
faq.answer: Generally, yes, Bukhara is considered safe, and many local vendors offer delicious and hygienic food. Look for places with high turnover, where food is cooked fresh in front of you. While restaurants are a safer bet, don't shy away from trying a well-established street shashlik stand if it looks clean and popular with locals. Always trust your gut.

faq.question: What's the best time of day to visit Lyabi-Hauz for dining?
faq.answer: While charming throughout the day, the best time to dine at Lyabi-Hauz is arguably in the late afternoon or early evening. As the sun begins to set, the temperature cools, and the ancient buildings glow in warm light. Many restaurants and chaykhanas come alive with soft lighting and a lively atmosphere, offering stunning photo opportunities.

faq.question: Are there vegetarian options available for shashlik or other dishes near Lyabi-Hauz?
faq.answer: While traditional shashlik is meat-based, many restaurants in Bukhara are increasingly offering vegetarian options, including vegetable shashlik (skewers of grilled vegetables like tomatoes, peppers, and onions). You'll also find a variety of fresh salads, vegetarian soups, and side dishes like bread and rice. Always ask if you have dietary restrictions.

methodology: Our selection for the best tea and shashlik spots near Lyabi-Hauz was curated through extensive local research, diner reviews, and expert culinary evaluations. Emphasis was placed on authenticity, atmosphere, quality of ingredients, and proximity to the iconic pool, ensuring a truly immersive Silk Road dining experience.
